key_area: Full Stack TypeScript Engineer (IC Technical, E1-E6) - Canonical

Canonical six-level IC ladder for engineers who own features end to end across UI, API, and data layers in a TypeScript-centered stack, consolidated by union from five independent blind generations; E3 Senior is the terminal level.

E1: Associate Full Stack Engineer
E2: Full Stack Engineer
E3: Senior Full Stack Engineer
E4: Staff Full Stack Engineer
E5: Senior Staff Full Stack Engineer
E6: Principal Full Stack Engineer

E1: task
E2: component
E3: capability / domain (terminal level)
E4: multiple teams
E5: organization
E6: company

E1: ships well-defined tasks across the stack with guidance and learns the stack
E2: independently delivers complete features spanning UI
E3: owns a product capability across the stack and sets the local bar
E4: drives technical outcomes across multiple teams and multiplies other engineers
E5: sets technical direction and standards for the organization
E6: shapes company-level technical strategy and represents engineering externally

key_attribute: Type System as a Design Tool
E1:
Depth: Writes correctly typed code without escape hatches (`any`-equivalents), uses the codebase's existing types and generics correctly, and reads compiler errors to the actual cause with guidance.

Evidenced by: Gets a compiler error on a discriminated-union narrowing case they haven't seen before, reads the message past the top line to find the actual mismatched member, and fixes the type rather than reaching for `as`.
E2:
Depth: Models feature domains so invalid states fail to compile — sum types / discriminated unions over boolean flags, narrowing over assertions — preferring type-level constraints where the compiler can carry the load.

Evidenced by: Turns a boolean-flag-soup form state (`isLoading`/`isError`/`hasData` that can all be true at once) into a discriminated union so the impossible combinations don't compile, without being told to.
E3:
Depth: Designs the shared domain types a capability is built on, keeping inference ergonomic for consumers; judges when type-level sophistication pays and when it obscures, and unwinds accumulated type erosion in others' code.

Evidenced by: Reviews a teammate's PR that adds a fourth optional field to an already-sprawling props type, and instead proposes (and lands) the discriminated-union refactor that makes the three valid variants explicit and the invalid ones uncompilable.
E4:
Depth: Sets type-design conventions multiple teams adopt — strictness policy, shared type libraries, branded identifiers, result types — and leads migrations that raise strictness without halting delivery.

Evidenced by: Publishes the branded-ID and Result-type conventions as the team's internal type-utilities package, with a codemod that migrated three existing services onto it without a delivery freeze.
E5:
Depth: Owns an organization's type-system posture — compiler baselines, monorepo type architecture, upgrade cadence — measured by defect and velocity outcomes.

Evidenced by: Sets the org's `strict`-mode and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` baseline for all new repos, tracked against a quarterly defect-rate dashboard leadership reviews.
E6:
Depth: Makes company-level language and type-platform bets and represents the practice externally (talks, upstream contributions, published patterns).

Evidenced by: Is the internal reviewer of record when the company adopts a new TypeScript major version, and publishes the migration's lessons as a conference talk that other companies cite.
